title: Card sits in the asset card, collapsed, with a count badge and nothing else
custom_preconds:
1. Sign in to the Maintenance Reminders QA build as an Owner/Admin (any user who can open Settings > Maintenance and create and edit work orders and customers).
  2. Open Settings > Maintenance. Open the schedule 'ZZAUTOTEST Highway Tractor PM', or create it with New schedule: add service 'PM-A' with a Calendar trigger of Every 6 months and canned lines, for example 'Engine oil and filter change' 0.8 hours, 'Chassis lubrication, 12 points' 0.5 hours, 'Air filter inspection' 0.3 hours and 'Brake adjustment check' 1.2 hours (4 lines, 2.8 hours). Save. Also add service 'PM-B' with a Calendar trigger of Every 12 months and its own canned lines.
  3. Open Customers > 'ZZAUTOTEST Fleet Co' > Assets, open unit 'ZZAUTOTEST 402' and its Maintenance tab; press Enroll in Schedule, choose 'ZZAUTOTEST Highway Tractor PM' and enter last service dates: PM-A about seven months ago (for example 6 Mar 2026) and PM-B a little under a year ago (for example 15 Oct 2025, so it falls due on 15 Oct 2026). Press Enroll. PM-A reads Overdue and PM-B Due soon.
  4. On the customer page press New Work Order, choose unit 'ZZAUTOTEST 402' and create the work order (it opens as an estimate). Note its number, for example S3780-15904.
custom_steps:
1. Open the work order and look at the asset card before expanding anything.
  2. Read the collapsed Maintenance schedule card: note everything it shows besides its badge.
  3. Press Expand and count the rows that read Due soon, Due today or Overdue. Compare with the badge.
  4. Collapse the card again.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • The maintenance card sits inside the asset card and is collapsed when the work order opens.
  • Collapsed, it carries a badge with the number of services that are due soon, due today or overdue: 2 here (PM-A overdue, PM-B due soon).
  • The badge stands alone: no service names, dates or other words appear beside it. The design shows the card title Maintenance schedule and the badge as 2 due; whether those words are allowed is an open product question, so write down exactly what you see and do not fail the case on it.
  • Because the card stays collapsed, a unit with many due services does not make the work order scroll on and on.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-3780 (Maintenance Reminders); story SV-10572 (S16, The maintenance panel on a work order); Chunk 2 MR (Confluence 897679389) as edited 5 October 2026, S16; read 6 Oct 2026. Source-verified 6 October 2026; not yet build-verified.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S16-R1: “The panel will sit inside the asset card and be collapsed by default”
  • S16-R2: “Collapsed, it will carry a badge counting the services that are due soon, due today or overdue. It carries the badge alone, with no other text”
  • S16-E2: “A unit with ten due services does not scroll forever, because the panel is collapsed by default”
